articles.title: JAL shares delist from BSE and NSE today: Will its 6.5 lakh shareholders get anything?
articles.content: Jaiprakash Associates shares were delisted from the BSE and NSE on Thursday, marking the closure of one of India's longest-running insolvency cases. The delisting follows the acquisition of the debt-laden company's assets by Adani Group. JAL said it had received final approval from both exchanges and thanked them for their support during its listing tenure.

articles.title: India-UK FTA levels the playing field for apparel exporters, says Pearl Global's Pallab Banerjee
articles.content: India's apparel exports are set for a significant boost with the new UK Free Trade Agreement, finally removing a long-standing 10-12% tariff disadvantage against competitors like Bangladesh and Cambodia. Industry leaders anticipate improved price competitiveness, attracting fresh investments, increasing exports, and creating substantial employment opportunities across various garment categories.

articles.title: Rupee falls 21 paise to 94.71 against US dollar in early trade
articles.content: The rupee depreciated 21 paise to 94.71 against the US dollar due to the US Federal Reserve's hawkish stance and a strong dollar index. Asian currencies also weakened, impacting the rupee. Meanwhile, positive sentiment emerged from reports of a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and ongoing trade talks between India and the US.

articles.title: US Fed's hawkish tone shuts door on India bond rally for now
articles.content: Indian government bonds saw a slight dip as the U.S. Federal Reserve adopted a more hawkish stance, signaling potential rate hikes this year due to persistent inflation risks. This shift influenced Treasury yields, while foreign investors continued to pour funds into Indian bonds, attracted by central bank measures.

articles.title: US Stock Market: Warsh signals overhaul of policy communications, skips rate projection in major shift

articles.title: Vedanta Power shares drop 3%, fall below listing price. What lies ahead?

articles.title: US Stock Market: Trump backs Fed Chair Warsh after rate hold, softens tone on monetary policy
articles.content: US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, a departure from his past criticisms of the central bank.  While the Fed kept rates steady, with some policymakers hinting at future hikes, Trump indicated he trusts Warsh's judgment.  Warsh, meanwhile, maintained a cautious stance on future rate movements and confirmed regular contact with the Treasury Secretary.

articles.title: HFCL shares jump 5% after Rs 2,666-crore RVNL order; stock soars 200% in 6 months
articles.content: HFCL shares surged after securing a significant contract from Rail Vikas Nigam Limited for the BharatNet project. This order strengthens HFCL's telecom network presence. The company is also expanding into defence and aerospace sectors. HFCL is a key player in optical fibre cable manufacturing and is involved in AI connectivity. Its export revenue is projected to grow substantially.
